I find the grey-text-swimming-in-ocean-of-whitespace look that's been spreading around the web of late to be essentially unusable. I like high information density, low visual complexity, minimal graphics, and clear, contrasty text. I normally use RES to disable all custom styles on Reddit, and installed a local style to reverse the readability-damaging change that Reddit made to line spacing a couple of months ago -- the one that added unnecessary extra whitespace between lines of paragraph text, so all of the text took up about 50% more space. It's great that Voat has a "disable custom subverse styles" in the server-side user preferences, but, unfortunately, the default style just isn't working for me (though I admit that night mode is an improvement).

I understand that a lot of people prefer the current interface style, but it would be very nice to have officially-supported interface configuration options for the default style -- sort of like what DuckDuckGo has for search results -- that offer the option of restoring a more traditional style. I'd love the ability to darken the text, reduce whitespace, shrink line spacing, turn off animations, etc., without having to rely on local user styles that might break whenever Voat's DOM changes. Maybe something as simple as regenerating and caching a new default CSS for logged-in users, based on options in they set in the preferences?
It has been confirmed that Voat will have customizable features, including UI adjustment abilities. Though, I'm unsure how it will be like, exactly.

So I'm getting a new computer in June, and I love CK1 and EU2, which new Paradox game should I get first?

Do you have a particular time period for combat that you enjoy?

If you like WWII- Go with Arsenal of Democracy or Hearts of Iron II. Hearts of Iron 3 was TOO complex, and I didn't really enjoy it. The interface was pretty annoying to use too. Just check for any operating system conflicts between your new rig and the two older titles. They are essentially the same game; I think AoD was a mod of HoI2, that got picked up for commercial release. Check Steam or GoG, they should both be relatively cheap.

If you're looking solely for a NEW Paradox game- I'd say EU4. It was pretty polished, I just think the diplomacy was a bit off. I still prefer EU3 Divine Wind for that reason. If you don't mind the older graphics, I think EU3 Divine Wind is a better game. CK2 I have, haven't played much. My heirs were all inbred mongrels. I'd avoid Victoria 2, the time period is kind of limited-unless you think you'd like a game where you basically modernize an economy for 150 years.

Best thing about Paradox games is that there are tons of mods out there- extends replayability for some time.

It's not the same type of game- but a surprising favorite of mine was Mount and Blade:Warband. There's supposed to be another one coming out soon- but who knows when. That's more of a medieval sandbox type of game, where you control one character and influence the world. Kind of like Skyrim mixed with a Paradox game. These games are mostly older- you can probably run them now on almost any rig that's post 2010.

A word more on EU4- my issue was that at times advancement for techs or what not depended upon what level my King had in certain areas (Diplomacy, Miltary etc.) I don't know if they've changed this at all- but essentially, if you had bad luck, or moronic despots...you were stuck until your King hit the genetic lottery.

Aside from that, and some issues with half the world declaring war on you at once- it is still a good game. I'm assuming they may have addressed some of these issues- but I don't know for sure.

They've changed some of the way monarch points worked since the initial release to address this specific complaint. It used to to be you had 0-6 of each from your leader and then 0-3 of each you could buy with advisers. Now there's an additional 0-1 from power projection, and you can choose a "national focus" to make up for areas where you leader is weak. I don't know if this is enough enough to convince you, but I certainly like it the way it is currently.

I assume with half the world declaring on you at once, that's the same as badboy/infamy from EU3, it's just counted differently (aggressive expansion). You still have to wait for it to burn off. And yes, there has been a lot of tweaking the values since release. Whether it's too little or too much for you I couldn't tell you, but it feels realistic to me. If I try and gobble up everyone people get pissed, but if I am careful about who I ally with and who I attack and I don't try to annex huge territories at once, it is very manageable.

That was the issue- Monarch points. Given what you've said, it's time to give it another look.

AE felt too vague in the game to get a feeling for- whereas badboy was a hard cap number, with some random events thrown in that could cost you points now and again. I grabbed it the day it came out played a month, and probably never went back. Current year is 2448 in my EU3 Divine Wind mod I made. HRE, Russia, China are the last of the big three (Like Oceania, Eurasia and Eastasia) and a mishmosh of European holdouts and independent American states survive in the North American hinterlands.

It may be time to nuke the world, and move on to the next generation of mutated remnants of society.

Any suggestion for a sci-fi or fantasy 4X strategy game? I'm reinstalling Civ IV right now because one of the expansions (Beyond the Sword I think) has fantasy and sci-fi mods, but any suggestions for dedicated games would be appreciated. Something that is easy to get into would be appreciated as well since I don''t play 4X games much.

Oldest ones I can think of would be Stelcon 2169, and Masters of Orion 1+2. Still worth playing any of em, IMHO. (One of the MOO's was really bad, 2 or 3, I can't remember.)

My suggestions for Fantasy:

Total War Medieval Kingdoms: The Third Age Mod- Set in the world of Middle Earth, this mod changes the game's units, locations and battlefields to the map of Middle Earth. Different races, units, battle scenes. Game is amazing with this mod. I only bought it for this reason. Took me a bit to get it running, but check out some videos if you've never seen this one before. Not EXACTLY 4x, but similar in theory. The battlefields are amazing. Nothing like storming the castle of Gondor with 1000 Orcs and trolls etc. at your command. Or replaying Helm's deep. I spent way too much time in that mod.

If you're going to play Civ 4 BTS anyway- Fall From Heaven is a must play. Definitely not bad.

Sci Fi- There's a Star Trek mod for Civ 4 BTS which wasn't bad. The Star Wars one never worked for me.

All these have the benefit of being free.

Distant worlds is a sci-fi strategy game set in outer space. It was amazingly deep and complex and last I heard there were some decent mods available. I'm an experienced strategy gamer- grew up playing Master of Orion 1 and 2 (which I recommend either if you're not a graphics snob), and that learning curve was a bit steep. It could be that I don't have the time to devote to figuring out the system- but the game looks beautiful.

Aside from that- The Heroes of Might and Magic series are turn based RPG style set in a fantasy world. Not exactly along the line of strategy, but a blend of strategy and turn based- but that basically opens up a whole new genre.

Galactic Civilizations II was great- and I think there's a third coming out. If it's still in early release- don't do it. Stop giving them money for unfinished products! That's a turn based space strategy simulation game. II is worth the money though. Maps are huge, and the game is infinitely replayable. Very similar to MOO.

Given your note about easy to get into, I don't even know where to begin- so many of these games are tough to start at first.

Since you're familiar with Civilization, Alpha Centauri might be a good place to start. I don't know enough about the new Civ-type space game to recommend it or not.

Fall from Heaven is the main reason I am reinstalling Civ 4 tonight, along with another mod that was included in BTS that moves the game to space (EDIT: it is Final Frontier, a built in mod for Civ IV BTS).

I've tried to play Alpha Centauri, but just could not get into it for some reason. I don''t think it was the graphics because that isn't something that normally bothers me, so I might try it again at some point.

Finally, I realized I already own GalCiv II (habitual bundle buyer), so I'm installing that now. Gal Civ III has quite mixed reviews citing stability issues and missing stuff from II, and hasn't dropped below $25, so I'll wait on that one if I like II and if it gets fixed. I put MOO 1+2 on my waitlist on isthereanydeal too, I'll check it out next time it goes on sale on GOG. Thanks for the suggestions.
